Fulesd Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Fülesd, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews settled in Fülesd in the 18th century, mostly in agriculture, and joined the Orthodox movement after Hungarian Jewry's Schism. Population held near 55 through the early 20th century. The community was too small to organize formally or afford a caretaker, instead paying a share of the Fehérgyarmat rabbinate's salary; by the 1941 Hungarian communities census, only 9 families remained, worshipping under a thatched-roof synagogue the community leader described as barely worth anything. In April 1944, residents were deported via Kölcse to the Mátészalka Ghetto - joining 17,000 other district Jews - enduring roughly a month of famine and mistreatment before deportation to Auschwitz. The synagogue survived the war undamaged; of its two preserved Torah scrolls, one went to the Fehérgyarmat Jewish community, the other to Israel. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1873, its newest to 1940.
